scopeReview: SPS-6.A.1–5: housing affordability and discrimination, environmental burdens, informal tenure, inclusionary housing/local food responses, renewal/gentrification tradeoffs and fragmented governance.
varietyReview: Four original assessed stimuli compare rent shares, tracked original households, mapped exposure and a fictional inclusionary rule. Additional distinct applications cover redlining, blockbusting, reinvestment evidence, tenure, renewal, food access and institutions.
repetitionReview: Avoids treating all turnover as forced displacement, every renovation as gentrification or all informal residents as one legal/social group. Numeric and conceptual tasks differ; all options explained and keys varied. Difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Official scope and primary HUD historical discrimination definitions checked. Original hypothetical accounts only; no actual lending assessment, legal advice, diagnosis, private data, third-party question or new student resource. Automated review is not independent human review.

questions.correctOption: A spends 30% and B spends 36%, so B has the higher rent-to-income share.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed.30/.36 and gap6 percentage points. Same monthly currency/net-income definition; no legal housing threshold, personalized advice or judgment about real households.

questions.correctOption: Exactly 400 original households are no longer present; their reasons for leaving require further evidence.
questions.independentReview: Independently verified1000−600=400 and400/1000=.4. Same original-household cohort; no household splitting/merging in this simplified account, and no count of newcomers.

questions.correctOption: The pattern warrants investigation of unequal environmental burdens, while individual outcomes and causes remain unmeasured.
questions.independentReview: Index is explicitly synthetic, not a pollutant concentration or medical threshold. Checked A70>B20 and avoided individual-income or racial inference from area means.
Calculated150*.2=30 exactly, no rounding or actual jurisdiction rule. Twenty percent explicitly refers to all project dwellings, avoiding floor-area/bedroom ambiguity.

questions.correctOption: Redlining that restricts credit through discriminatory neighborhood classification.
questions.independentReview: Historical discriminatory mechanism checked against primary HUD training; applicants explicitly otherwise eligible. No current legal advice or assertion of sole causation by HOLC maps.
Avoided repeating discriminatory claims as facts. Broker’s manipulation, not racial identity or actual value decline, defines the mechanism; fictional historical example.

questions.correctOption: Reinvestment and housing-cost trends together with resident and business turnover and social-composition evidence.
questions.independentReview: Distinguishes renovation, reinvestment and social change without defining all urban improvement as displacement. Same-household linkage and causality remain separate questions.

questions.correctOption: Secure tenure depends on recognized rights and institutions, not only the physical condition of a building.
questions.independentReview: No real legal-status determination, stigmatizing criminality claim or advice. Squatter/informal settlement relation stated through varied tenure, consistent with official A.2.

questions.correctOption: Physical upgrades can coexist with relocation costs and disrupted social networks, so both outcomes require assessment.
questions.independentReview: Conditional tradeoff not a conclusion about an actual renewal program. Distinguishes aggregate assets from distribution and lived experience.

questions.correctOption: Prices, operating times, usable travel routes and the foods available relative to residents’ needs.
questions.independentReview: Focuses on local-food response in urban A.3, not duplicating agricultural yield or nutrition requirements. No dietary or medical recommendation.

questions.correctOption: Fragmented authority can hinder coordinated responses to problems that cross jurisdictions.
questions.independentReview: Direct A.5 alignment, no assertion of one legally required institutional structure or that regional government always resolves conflict.
